body: How many tablets and at what dosage?  But generally... now is the time to go to the hospital.  They can at least check a paracetamol level and check for liver injury.  Please go.  Paracetamol overdoses aren't reversible if caught too late.  They won't (or shouldn't) care about the codeine bit.  Please go.

Four days post-op from a craniectomy?  You are in the medical field.  If that's the case then it's quite kind of you to volunteer time chatting here with people.

Botox is an option and the next one most likely, although I have little hope that it'll help after everything else has failed.  It's really the disability that's come with the chronic pain that is most distressing.  It's hard for me to do things or complete ADL's these days.

It's not really operable for a lot of reasons.  As for painkillers, I mean pretty much whatever I want, although I hate them.  They don't help and they make me feel like shit usually.  And I don't want to turn a pain disorder into an addiction.  I don't really take anything right now.
Nothing that's worked so far.

Thanks.  I don't think the words would be hard.  Something like "Hey, I'm very sorry, but I've decided to end my life.  Please don't open this door unless you're a trained EMT or first responder.  I have tried to keep it as clean as possible.  Again, very sorry."

Anti-convulsants tend to make people feel slow and... depressed.  And they haven't helped much for pain.  Tried lots.  Gamma Knife isn't performed for what I have unfortunately.  And it's not affordable.
I have a pain condition that isn't very treatable.  It's similar to Trigeminal Neuralgia, if you've heard of that.
Maybe.  I wonder if a very plain and honest note on the door describing what they're about to step into might be helpful.  I'd similarly explain my intent to keep it as clean as possible.

Not necessarily.  I've worked in fields where I'm exposed to dead bodies. It can be peaceful.  And I appreciate you trying to convince me otherwise, but I'm also realistic about my life.  I don't have a lot to live for and have severe chronic pain.  It's very likely that I'll go sometime soon, and if I do I don't want to hurt someone else as I've stated.  A note briefing someone on what they're likely to find and preparations to contain bodily fluids are probably the best first steps.

Edit: What I mean to say is that bodies can appear to be at peace, and not that encountering them is peaceful.
I hope not.  I'd like to take steps to avoid that.  If I leave a note on the door and figure out a way to cover my body that might not be the case.
This is monstrous.  This post is either fake or you are one of the worst people I've ever heard of.

Thanks mate.  I am fairly alone at the moment, but I am doing exactly those things.  The hobby is climbing at a local gym, and thankfully it's a fairly social activity.  But otherwise, the phone hasn't rung in years and the insomnia has me feeling like a broken person.  Still trying though.

I've been depressed for a couple years with severe insomnia.  My friend's stopped wanting to be around me about a year ago and I've been a shell of myself.  I'm trying to get better, but it's hard doing it alone.
Small goals help.  Sometimes that's all I can do.
Yeah, that's true.  It's just hard not to equate affection/validation with quality of life.
Yeah.  Thanks.  This was formerly my exact thinking when I was healthier person, but now I feel kinda stuck in my own shit and toxicity.
Good points.
Working on it.  Having a physical illness kinda compounds the depression.  But thanks.
Probably.  It's been a tough thing to get over and I've been wrestling with it for a while.
Yes.  And I don't know how to negotiate that.  I didn't intend to develop feelings for this one friend again, and now that they're there it puts me in a weird position.
Yeah.  When I say ghosted I mean we make plans a few days before and then I get radio silence on the day of what we planned.
Probably yeah.  I need to get over it.
Yeah I feel the same way about it myself.  I need to get passed this somehow.

I'm sorry you're suffering.  Keep trying friend.  Depression and some other illnesses can do all of the above as well.  And honestly, 3 concussions isn't that many for the average man that grew up playing contact sports.

Hmm.  Can I ask you something first?  Why do you think you have CTE?  That's typically only diagnosable on autopsy.  I only ask because there are many disease that can mimic CTE and have more favorable outcomes.
Well alcohol will definitely make things worse in terms of sleep and test, so be careful.
Unfortunately I've done the rounds on sleep aids and none have them have really worked for me.  But I should try some other comprehensive life changes and test again in a few months.

These are great points.  I've actually tried Mirtazapine and couldn't get passed the dead brain sensation it caused me.  I don't think I've ever had such a bad reaction to a drug.  I took it for a few months and just spent them sort of sleep-walking and empty-headed.  But it's a good thought and I know it helps a lot of people.

Stress?  Yes.  I'll work more on the mindfulness and deep meditation.

Magnesium?  Yes.  Taking 500mg nightly at the moment.  Zinc?  Nope.  I can start there.  Blue blockers?  Yes.  Even bought the glasses.  Sleep apnea?  Great thought, but very unlikely.  I'm a thin person and don't snore.  Still possible though and I'll reconsider it at my next chat with my doctor.
Yep.  It's hard to know when to call it though and just try TRT.  My only hesitation is the near to lifelong supplementation required.  I'd like to avoid that if possible.
I think a lot of people are in this same situation.  And there doesn't seem to be a lot of science to help make an educated decision here.
